body_markdown:
Sending frequent, low-value payments to a global workforce breaks traditional banking workflows. Our position: data labeling teams should buy a payouts API that bundles onboarding, tax, and real time payments under one contract, because stitching separate tools together costs more than any single fee line. You'll lose money to high conversion fees and risk compliance fines if you skip mandatory KYC (Know Your Customer) identity checks on your international contributors. Foreign contributors also need a[W-8BEN](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-8-ben) (foreign status certification form) on file before the first payout, or the default 30% withholding can apply to their US-sourced income. Compare the options below on that basis to find the right fit for global mass payments without the manual overhead.


**TLDR:**


- Compensating global data labelers requires routing micropayments without steep FX markups.
- You need providers offering local currency settlement and built-in KYC verification steps.
- Tipalti takes 1 to 5 days to clear transfers while applying FX markups up to 3.5%.
- The Dots API routes instant payouts across 190 countries with automated tax collection.


## What Are Payout Services for Data Labeling Companies?


Payout services for data labeling and expert networks route the financial logistics of compensating distributed global contributors. Building accurate models requires[massive contributor pools](https://encord.com/blog/automated-data-annotation-guide/) . This scale forces your business to send small, frequent payments across many countries. You must clear funds through local payment networks while avoiding steep foreign exchange markups.


The friction extends beyond routing money across borders. You must also collect mandatory tax forms and run KYC (Know Your Customer) identity checks before that first payout clears. Reliable payout services automate this compliance stack, letting your team scale without adding manual back-office paperwork.


## How We Ranked Payout Services


Selecting a payout provider requires infrastructure built for high-volume, cross-border transfers. We researched public documentation, fee schedules, and feature sets across top options, relying on verifiable public data.


We compared each provider against these core requirements:


- Country routing to reach global data labelers.
- Payout methods (payment rails, the networks that move money) that settle funds in local currencies.
- Settlement speed with a preference for instant processing.
- Identity verification with built-in KYC (Know Your Customer) steps during onboarding.
- Tax automation to file 1099s (US tax forms) and handle[foreign contractor withholding tax](https://usedots.com/blog/guide-to-us-tax-withholding-for-foreign-contractors/) via W-8BENs (foreign status certification forms).
- Transparent fee models without hidden foreign exchange markups.

## Stripe


Stripe Connect delivers standard payment infrastructure for data labeling teams.


### What They Offer


- Routes funds to users across 46 supported countries.
- Automates KYC collection.


Good for: This service fits businesses accepting card payments in core markets.


Limitation: Stripe charges a[1 to 1.5% fee](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/instant-payouts) for each Instant Payout attempt. The service restricts these faster transfers to supported debit cards in nine core regions and caps them at ten per day. Every cross-border flow also adds a 1% foreign exchange surcharge. These layered costs and daily transfer limits restrict volume when compensating a global workforce of data labelers.


## Tipalti


Tipalti is an accounts payable automation suite built for batch processing supplier invoices.


### What They Offer


- Connects finance departments to 50 local and international rails.
- Processes standard batch ACH transfers for recurring vendor billing.


Good for: Tipalti suits finance units focused on automating back-office vendor payments.


Limitation: The service relies on transfers taking 1 to 5 days and applies[Tipalti FX fees](https://usedots.com/blog/tipalti-reviews-pricing-alternatives/) of up to 3.5%.


Bottom line: Tipalti handles traditional invoices, but Dots fits data labeling organizations better by delivering immediate settlement without hidden FX markups.


## Payoneer


Payoneer is a cross-border payment provider helping data labeling companies route funds to international freelancers.


### What They Offer


- Routes payments across borders and converts funds into multiple local currencies.
- Holds international earnings in a standalone digital wallet before local withdrawal.


Good for: This provider suits independent contractors wanting a dedicated account for their earnings.


Limitation: Moving money to a local bank requires the contributor to initiate an extra withdrawal step from a standalone digital wallet. This added friction delays final settlement for data labelers who need immediate access to their earnings. Forcing payees to route funds through a proprietary ecosystem complicates the payout lifecycle.


## Hyperwallet


Backed by PayPal, Hyperwallet operates as an enterprise payout system distributing funds across[200 markets](https://www.paypal.com/us/business/make-payments/enterprise-payouts) .


### What They Offer


- Distributes global payouts directly through their native ecosystem.
- Supports 9 distinct withdrawal methods for payees.
- Includes transfer options like direct bank deposits, PayPal, Venmo, prepaid cards, and direct to debit.


Good for: Large corporate enterprises operating exclusively within PayPal.


Limitation: With only nine standard withdrawal methods, many international contributors must route their earnings through a PayPal account to reach their local bank. This additional transfer step adds processing time before funds finally clear. Your data labelers experience delayed settlement instead of receiving immediate access to their compensation.


## Trolley


Trolley operates as a tax and payout suite moving money internationally using standard banking networks.


### What They Offer


- Routes international payments across 210 countries using standard banking infrastructure.
- Gathers basic tax forms to support contractor compliance tracking.


Good for: This service fits businesses running standard monthly payroll batches without needing broader coverage, which is why some teams review[Trolley alternatives](https://usedots.com/trolley-alternative/) .


Limitation: The service relies on standard banking networks without instant settlement capabilities, and provides a limited number of payout methods compared to API-first solutions.

### How do you choose between Dots, Stripe Connect, and Tipalti for global data labeling payouts?


Base your decision on required country coverage, settlement speed, and foreign exchange fees. Pick Stripe Connect for core markets, Tipalti for standard accounts payable batches, or Dots to reach 190 countries with instant settlement.

Yes, Dots settles disbursements immediately across 300 local payout methods after you approve a batch. Tipalti relies on standard transfers that take 1 to 5 days to clear and apply foreign exchange markups up to 3.5%.


### What makes Payoneer and Hyperwallet different from Dots for contributor withdrawals?


Payoneer and Hyperwallet route funds through proprietary digital wallets or a narrow set of withdrawal methods. Dots lets your data labelers receive earnings directly through 300 local payment networks without requiring a standalone wallet.
